binders: First claim: for every type Omega with a measurable-space structure, every measure mu on Omega that has total mass one, and every function X: Omega -> Real.
Second claim: for every type Omega with a measurable-space structure, every measure mu on Omega (not assumed to be a probability measure), and every function X: Omega -> Real.
Third claim: for every real parameter lambda.
Fourth claim: for every nonnegative real rate (including rate zero).
hypotheses: In the first claim, there exist a LocalDef009 tag i different from the fifth/linear-MGF tag LocalDef010 and a real K>0 such that X satisfies the formulation selected by i at scale K.

Equivalently, the first antecedent may be witnessed by any one of: a Gaussian tail bound 2 exp(-t^2/K^2); sqrt(p)-moment growth (integral |X|^p <= (K sqrt(p))^p); square-exponential control over |lambda|<=1/K; or one-point integrability with integral exp(X^2/K^2)<=2. Each selected predicate also requires measurability and K>0, with its stated integrability conditions.
In the second claim, X is measurable.
conclusions: Under the first claim's antecedent, there exists a real K>0 such that X satisfies the fixed sub-exponential moment formulation: X is measurable and almost-everywhere measurable, and for every real p>=1, |X|^p (real rpow) is integrable and its integral is at most (K p)^p.
For measurable X under an arbitrary measure, the exponential gauge of X^2 is finite if and only if the square-exponential gauge of X is finite.
For the same X, the exponential gauge of X^2 equals the square of the square-exponential gauge of X, as an equality in ENNReal.
For the exponential distribution of positive rate lambda, the integral of x is 1/lambda, the variance of x is 1/lambda^2, and the exponential gauge of x is ENNReal.ofReal(2/lambda).
For every nonnegative real rate, the exponential gauge of the identity function under the pushforward to Real of the Poisson law on Nat is strictly below ENNReal infinity.
mathematical_definitions: The exponential gauge G1_mu(Y) is inf {t in ENNReal : Y is measurable, t != 0, t != infinity, exp(|Y|/t.toReal) is integrable, and integral exp(|Y|/t.toReal) dmu <= 2}.
The square-exponential gauge G2_mu(X) is the infimum of ENNReal scales t such that X is measurable, t is nonzero and finite, exp(X^2/t.toReal^2) is integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
The real-cast Poisson measure of rate r is the pushforward of the Poisson measure on Nat along n |-> (n:Real).
The exponential measure of parameter lambda is the gamma measure with shape 1 and rate lambda.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The proposition simultaneously asserts: (1) on every probability space, if a real random variable satisfies at some positive scale any of four indexed sub-Gaussian conditions other than the centered linear-MGF condition, then it satisfies at some positive scale the sub-exponential moment bound integral |X|^p <= (K p)^p for every real p>=1; (2) for every measurable real function under any measure, the exponential gauge of X^2 is finite exactly when the square-exponential gauge of X is finite, and in fact G1_mu(X^2)=G2_mu(X)^2; (3) an exponential random variable of positive rate lambda has mean 1/lambda, variance 1/lambda^2, and exponential gauge 2/lambda viewed in ENNReal; and (4) the exponential gauge of a real-valued Poisson random variable is finite for every nonnegative rate.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The first implication excludes the fifth tag, namely the centered linear-MGF formulation, so it does not claim that formulation implies the fixed sub-exponential moment formulation through this antecedent.
Only the first claim assumes mu is a probability measure. The gauge identity in the second claim quantifies over arbitrary measures.

The second claim assumes only measurability of X. If an admissible-scale set is empty, its ENNReal infimum may be infinity; the finiteness equivalence explicitly permits both sides to be non-finite, while the equality remains an unconditional ENNReal equality.
Admissible gauge scales explicitly exclude both zero and infinity before converting the scale to Real.
The moment formulations quantify over real p>=1 and use real rpow, not merely integer moments.

The tail predicates use Measure.real, which converts an infinite ENNReal measure value to zero. In the first claim the probability-measure assumption prevents tail-event measures from being infinite, but the predicate itself does not encode that safeguard.
The outer existential K>0 in the first conclusion duplicates the positivity already included in the selected moment predicate.
The exponential-distribution identities require lambda>0; no claim is made there for nonpositive parameters.
The Poisson finiteness claim includes rate zero because its binder is NNReal and has no strict-positivity hypothesis; it asserts finiteness only, not a closed-form gauge value.
